A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the synthesis of Fe-Au core–shell nanocrystals with an original faceted morphology has been achieved through a simple physical route, and the remarkable stability of this morphology is attributed to the low elastic energy resulting from a weak misfit at the interface compared to the high surface energy contribution.
we have shown the importance of the elastic energy in the formation of core-shell nanocrystals with an original shape.

the synthesis of the fully crystalline faceted Fe-Au core–shell nanoparticles has been achieved by a physical route and the stability of these nanoparticles was investigated by the finite-element method, and the results are in excellent agreement with the experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphology of Fe-Au core–shell nanoparticles is determined by the interplay of elastic and surface energies.
the core-shell morphology is not only a function of the misfit at the interface but also depends on the surface energy anisotropy of the core and shell.
the morphology of the nanoparticles can be tuned to optimize their stability.
